_readme: Closes the checkpoint gap identified across Chapters 2-9. Intentionally NOT covered here (matching the pattern already used for 1.0/1.1/1.2/2.0/3.0/etc.): chapter intro sections and pure class-discussion sections, which don't carry new factual content to check.

quizzes.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three jobs money does, according to this section?
options: Medium of exchange
Unit of account
Guarantee of employment

quizzes.question: What distinguishes 'representative money' from 'commodity money'?
options: Representative money is a claim on a commodity held elsewhere, rather than having value from the material itself
Representative money can only be used online
There is no real difference between the two

quizzes.question: According to this section, what does money that reliably holds its value tend to encourage?
options: Immediate spending over saving
Saving and long-term thinking, since patience isn't punished by lost value
Higher time preference across the board

quizzes.question: Why did shells sometimes fail as a form of early money?
options: They were too heavy to carry
They could sometimes be found too easily nearby, undermining their scarcity
They were illegal in most societies

quizzes.question: What tradeoff does this section highlight in the shift from cash to cards and phone-based money?
options: Cards are always more expensive to use than cash
Access to your own money now depends entirely on a bank's systems and permission
There is no real tradeoff — it's a pure improvement

quizzes.question: What's actually new about the kind of digital currency Bitcoin represents, compared to digital bank ledgers that already existed?
options: Digital money that doesn't depend on any single company or government to issue or control it
Bitcoin was the first digital record of any kind
Bitcoin removed the need for the internet

quizzes.question: What institutions typically hold the authority to create new money in a fiat system?
options: Individual citizens by majority vote
A central bank and government treasury
Any registered business

quizzes.question: What determines the money supply in a fiat system, according to this section?
options: A fixed mathematical formula nobody can change
Policy decisions made by central banking institutions
The total weight of gold held in national reserves

quizzes.question: How does a CBDC differ from the digital money most people already use today?
options: It would be issued and controlled directly by a central bank, rather than existing as commercial bank deposits
It cannot be spent online
It is identical to Bitcoin in every respect

quizzes.question: In the example given, what happens to a R100 grocery basket after two years of 10% annual inflation?
options: It stays at R100
It costs R121
It costs exactly R120

quizzes.question: What two connected problems does this section say compound the effects of inflation?
options: Growing debt at every level of the economy, and a widening wealth gap between asset owners and non-owners
Rising unemployment and falling literacy rates
Higher taxes and slower internet speeds

quizzes.question: Why can't people who don't own appreciating assets protect their savings from inflation, according to this section?
options: They can, easily, by working harder
Money saved in cash or a standard bank account quietly loses value each year, with no built-in protection
Only wealthy people are affected by inflation at all

quizzes.question: How do many governments service large, growing debt loads, according to this section?
options: By fully paying it down within a year
Often by creating more currency, which feeds back into the inflation problem
Debt is not a real issue for governments

quizzes.question: What core question did the community described in this section start asking?
options: Could money be redesigned so no single institution held this much power over it?
How can banks be made more profitable?
Should gold replace paper currency again?

quizzes.question: What did the Cypherpunks argue was required for privacy and financial freedom in the digital age?
options: Government oversight of all transactions
Strong cryptography that didn't depend on trusting a bank, government, or company to behave well
A return to purely physical cash

quizzes.question: What is the key difference between a centralized and a decentralized system, as described here?
options: A centralized system has one party making decisions; a decentralized system spreads that authority across many independent participants
Decentralized systems are always faster than centralized ones
There is no meaningful difference

quizzes.question: Under what name was the Bitcoin whitepaper published in October 2008?
options: Craig Wright
Satoshi Nakamoto, a pseudonym — the real identity remains unknown
The Cypherpunk Collective

quizzes.question: How does Bitcoin's blockchain differ from a traditional bank's ledger?
options: Thousands of independent computers each keep an identical copy and agree on updates together, instead of one company keeping the official record
It is kept by a single, government-appointed company
It only exists on paper

quizzes.question: Which group is responsible for independently verifying that Bitcoin's rules are being followed?
options: Miners only
Full nodes
Central banks

quizzes.question: What question does this section ask directly, building on Chapter 2?
options: Does Bitcoin actually have the properties of good money?
Is gold better than Bitcoin in every way?
Should Bitcoin be banned?

quizzes.question: How was Bitcoin's design approach to sound-money properties different from gold's?
options: Bitcoin was designed from scratch with these properties as explicit goals, informed by where earlier forms of money fell short
Bitcoin ignored the properties of sound money entirely
Gold and Bitcoin were designed by the same process

quizzes.question: What is the main tradeoff to weigh across the three ways of acquiring bitcoin covered in this section?
options: Speed, privacy, and how much you need to trust a third party
Only the color of the app icon
There is no meaningful difference between them

quizzes.question: Why might physical peer-to-peer trading be an accessible entry point in a community like Ekasi?
options: It doesn't require a bank account or ID verification with a distant company
It is the only legal way to acquire bitcoin
It requires owning a centralized exchange account first

quizzes.question: What protects both sides during an online peer-to-peer bitcoin trade?
options: Nothing — it is entirely based on trust
Escrow services
A government regulator

quizzes.question: What does a Bitcoin wallet actually hold, according to this section?
options: Physical bitcoin coins
The private keys that prove you control certain bitcoin recorded on the blockchain
A copy of the entire blockchain

quizzes.question: What's the main difference between on-chain and Lightning wallets?
options: On-chain wallets deal directly with the base blockchain (better for savings); Lightning wallets use a faster, cheaper layer for everyday spending
Lightning wallets cannot receive any bitcoin
On-chain wallets are always custodial

quizzes.question: Why does open-source wallet software matter, according to this section?
options: It's required by law in most countries
The code is publicly available for anyone to inspect and verify, rather than requiring trust in the developer's word
It makes wallets load faster

quizzes.question: Why does this section stress that saving in bitcoin isn't risk-free?
options: Because bitcoin's price is genuinely volatile in the short term, even though many treat it as long-term protection against inflation
Because bitcoin cannot legally be saved
Because it's actually completely risk-free

quizzes.question: What does 'Don't Trust, Verify' mean in practice, according to this section?
options: Independently verifying claims yourself — checking block explorers, reading source code — rather than taking any single source's word for it
Never using a Bitcoin wallet without government approval
Trusting only Bitcoin Ekasi's official statements

quizzes.question: What determines the different 'flavors' of Lightning wallets, according to this section?
options: Who holds the keys and channels
The wallet's color scheme
Which country issued them

quizzes.question: What does open-source Lightning wallet software allow, same as in Chapter 7?
options: The community can verify the code actually does what it claims
It removes the need for any wallet at all
It guarantees the wallet is custodial

quizzes.question: Why might someone start with a custodial Lightning wallet before moving to self-custody?
options: Custodial setups are typically much simpler, while self-custodial ones involve managing channel liquidity and backups
Self-custodial wallets are illegal for beginners
There is no difference in setup complexity

quizzes.question: What is a Lightning 'invoice'?
options: A QR code generated by the receiver that the sender scans to pay
A monthly bill for using Bitcoin
A government tax form

quizzes.question: What advantage does a Lightning payment plugin give an online merchant, according to this section?
options: Near-instant payment with no chargeback risk
Automatic tax exemption
Free advertising from the payment processor

quizzes.question: How many merchants does Bitcoin Ekasi's EkasiPay network cover across Mossel Bay, according to this section?
What role do Bitcoin-linked gift cards and prepaid cards play, according to this section?
options: A bridge for people still getting comfortable with Lightning directly
They replace Lightning wallets entirely
They are only usable outside South Africa

quizzes.question: What does the pairing of public and private keys make possible, according to this section?
options: Self-custody without needing a central authority to verify who owns what
Unlimited free transactions
Automatic recovery of a lost wallet

quizzes.question: What is the key difference between a node and a miner, according to this section?
options: Nodes verify that rules are followed; miners propose new blocks of transactions — distinct roles, even if one computer can do both
They are exactly the same thing with two different names
Only miners are allowed to hold bitcoin

quizzes.question: What happens to Bitcoin's mining difficulty roughly every two weeks?
options: It resets to zero
It adjusts automatically to keep new blocks arriving about every 10 minutes, regardless of total mining power
It is set manually by a vote among miners

quizzes.question: According to this section, what must happen before a block is accepted into the blockchain?
options: Every node must independently verify the block follows every rule
Only the miner who created it needs to approve it
A central authority must sign off on it
